# Results -- Study 292 (Bitcoin-Hashrate) on real monthly tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: join the
curated month-end hash-rate series (EH/s) to the BTC-USD monthly close, regress
next-month BTC return on this month's hash-rate growth (with and without a
price-momentum control), and backtest the folk "long when hashrate rises" timing
rule against buy-and-hold. One-month execution lag; 30 bps one-way costs; long-only
(no borrow); price-only returns (BTC pays no yield).*
**Single-survivor bias**: BTC is the one crypto that survived and ~1000x'd; the
hash-rate / price co-trend is conditioned on that survival -- all timing results
benefit mechanically.* As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Shape | Fingerprint |
|--------|--------|-------|-------------|
| Curated hashrate (Blockchain.com, digitised) | 2014-01-31 -> 2026-05-31 | 149 months (EH/s) | `a4e6f7055e35` |
| yfinance BTC-USD monthly (adj close) | 2014-09-30 -> 2026-05-31 | 147 aligned months | (set on fetch) |

Both series trend up over the sample (hash rate ~0.01 -> ~1140 EH/s; BTC ~$400 ->
~$100k), so the analysis is done in **growth rates**, never levels, to avoid the
spurious-regression trap.

## Primary specification -- predictive regression of next-month return on hashrate growth

`r(t+1) = a + b * hashrate_growth(t) + e`

| Lookback | Slope b | HAC *t* | R^2 | n |
|----------|---------|---------|-----|---|
| 1 month  | -0.008  | **-0.05** | 0.000 | 147 |
| 3 months | +0.107  | +1.52   | 0.02  | 145 |
| 6 months | +0.181  | +1.74   | 0.03  | 142 |

**No horizon clears the inference bar (HAC *t* >= 2).** The 1-month slope is
statistically zero; the multi-month versions creep up only because longer-window
hash-rate growth becomes a slow trend filter that overlaps with price trend.

## Horse race -- does hashrate add anything beyond BTC's own momentum?

`r(t+1) = a + b * hashrate_growth(t) + c * price_momentum(t)`

| Regressor | HAC *t* |
|-----------|---------|
| Hashrate growth | **-0.07** |
| BTC price momentum | +0.83 |

Once BTC's own one-month momentum is in the regression, the hash-rate slope
collapses to zero. Whatever weak co-movement existed was already inside the price
trend -- **hashrate is redundant**.

## Timing rule (folk "long when hashrate rises") vs buy-and-hold

| Strategy | CAGR-ish (ann) | Ann. Sharpe | HAC *t* | Exposure |
|----------|----------------|-------------|---------|----------|
| Hashrate timing (net 30 bps) | +82.8%/yr | **+0.94** | +2.87 | long 86.5% of months |
| **Buy-and-hold BTC** | **+94.0%/yr** | **+1.04** | +3.35 | always long |
| Timing - buy-hold | **-11.2%/yr** | -- | (negative) | -- |

The timing rule earns a fortune in *absolute* terms only because it is long a
1000x asset 86% of the time -- and it still **underperforms buy-and-hold** on
both CAGR and Sharpe, because the months it sits in cash tend to be exactly the
sharp recovery months. Average turnover is only 0.19/mo (the signal rarely
flips), so costs are not the killer -- the *missed upside* is.

## Hash-Ribbons crossover (3/6-month MA, the "miner capitulation" trigger)

| Strategy | CAGR-ish (ann) | Ann. Sharpe | Exposure |
|----------|----------------|-------------|----------|
| Hash-Ribbons net 30 bps | +106.5%/yr | +1.23 | long 94% of months |

Higher absolute return -- but only because it is long *even more* of the time. As
exposure -> 100%, the rule converges to buy-and-hold. There is no skill being
added; the "signal" is just a long-bias dial.

## Sub-period sanity (timing-rule net annualised)

| Period | Net ann. |
|--------|----------|
| 2014-2017 | +120%/yr |
| 2018-2021 | +70%/yr |
| 2022-2026 | +45%/yr |

Returns decline as BTC's own returns decline -- the rule has no independent edge,
it simply tracks the asset.

## Positive control -- the engine detects a planted lead-lag

On the deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_series`) where last-month
hash-rate growth is *planted* into this-month price return (`beta=0.60`):

| Planted beta | Slope b | HAC *t* |
|--------------|---------|---------|
| 0.00 (null)  | -0.012  | -0.10   |
| +0.60        | +0.588  | **+5.13** |

The regression recovers a real lead-lag at *t* = 5.13 when one exists and reads
~zero on the null. The machinery is truthful -- the real tape simply has no
hashrate -> price predictive content.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** Hash-rate growth does not predict next-month BTC returns
  (HAC *t* = -0.05 at 1 month; no horizon clears *t* >= 2). In a horse race
  against BTC's own price momentum the hashrate slope collapses to *t* = -0.07.
  The level co-movement everyone points at is a shared up-trend (spurious in
  levels). Causality runs price -> hashrate (miners switch on when BTC is
  expensive), not the reverse. **NONE.**
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** The "long when hashrate rises" rule looks
  spectacular (+83%/yr) only because it is long a 1000x survivor 86% of the
  time, and it *still loses to buy-and-hold* (Sharpe 0.94 vs 1.04) net of costs.
  The Hash-Ribbons variant "wins" only by being long even more. No incremental
  edge survives the one benchmark that matters. **MIRAGE.**
- **Survivorship -- named.** BTC is the surviving crypto moonshot; the hash-rate
  co-trend is conditioned on that survival. Every long-biased result is an upper
  bound that would not have been knowable ex ante.
